reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling's 38 MW of disclosed IT capacity places it mid-scale in Virginia, where it accounts for 2.4 percent of the state's published data center load.

The facility spans 700,000 square feet and ranks 13th among the 25 Virginia data centers that publish capacity figures. Those 25 sites total 1,603 MW, so Sterling is a modest contributor to the disclosed total. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but the vast majority publish no capacity number, which means the state's true IT load is not visible from these figures alone.

For AI workloads, the 38 MW could support roughly 950 racks at a 40 kW per rack density, but the facility publishes no certifications, so its qualification for any particular workload class is not stated. Its suitability score of 69 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing from the record. The local grid's ability to absorb new load is not stated, so Sterling's role in AI scaling depends on factors outside this facility's published profile.
